content.stem: A random sample of $400$ residents of a city was surveyed, and $62\%$ of them said they support building a new public library. The margin of error for this estimate is $5$ percentage points. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is plausible that between $57\%$ and $67\%$ of all city residents support building the library.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exactly $62\%$ of all city residents support building the library.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Between $57\%$ and $67\%$ of the $400$ surveyed residents support building the library.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is likely that fewer than half of all city residents support building the library.

content.explanation: A random sample estimates the whole population, and the margin of error gives a range of plausible values for it: $62\% \pm 5\%$, or $57\%$ to $67\%$ of all residents.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: A sample gives an estimate with uncertainty, not an exact value for the population.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: The percent for the 400 surveyed residents is known exactly, $62\%$; the margin of error applies to the whole population.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: The entire plausible range, $57\%$ to $67\%$, is above $50\%$.
